claim: The committed step of eukaryotic DNA replication occurs when the pairs of Mcm2-7 replicative helicases that license each replication origin are activated.
source: The committed step of eukaryotic DNA replication occurs when the pairs of Mcm2-7 replicative helicases that license each replication origin are activated.
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract that draws on established knowledge about eukaryotic DNA replication mechanisms.

claim: Helicase activation requires the recruitment of Cdc45 and GINS to Mcm2-7, forming Cdc45-Mcm2-7-GINS complexes (CMGs).
source: Helicase activation requires the recruitment of Cdc45 and GINS to Mcm2-7, forming Cdc45-Mcm2-7-GINS complexes (CMGs).
evidence: This statement is supported by established knowledge in the field and is presented as background information.

claim: Cdc45 and GINS are recruited to loaded Mcm2-7 in two stages.
source: Using single-molecule biochemical assays to monitor CMG formation, we found that Cdc45 and GINS are recruited to loaded Mcm2-7 in two stages.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study's single-molecule experiments.

claim: Initially, Cdc45, GINS, and likely additional proteins are recruited to unstructured Mcm2-7 N-terminal tails in a Dbf4-dependent kinase (DDK)-dependent manner, forming Cdc45-tail-GINS intermediates (CtGs).
source: Initially, Cdc45, GINS, and likely additional proteins are recruited to unstructured Mcm2-7 N-terminal tails in a Dbf4-dependent kinase (DDK)-dependent manner, forming Cdc45-tail-GINS intermediates (CtGs).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study describing a novel intermediate complex.

claim: DDK phosphorylation of multiple phosphorylation sites on the Mcm2-7 tails modulates the number of CtGs formed per Mcm2-7.
source: DDK phosphorylation of multiple phosphorylation sites on the Mcm2-7 tails modulates the number of CtGs formed per Mcm2-7.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study based on experimental observations.

claim: In a second, inefficient event, a subset of CtGs transfer their Cdc45 and GINS components to form CMGs.
source: In a second, inefficient event, a subset of CtGs transfer their Cdc45 and GINS components to form CMGs.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study describing the conversion of CtGs to CMGs.

claim: Higher CtG multiplicity increases the frequency of CMG formation.
source: Importantly, higher CtG multiplicity increases the frequency of CMG formation.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study showing a correlation between CtG number and CMG formation efficiency.

claim: Two copies of the Mcm2-7 helicase are loaded around origin DNA as a head-to-head double hexamer during G1 phase.
source: Replisome assembly begins during G1 phase when two copies of the Mcm2-7 helicase are loaded around origin DNA as a head-to-head double hexamer (Yardimci and Walter, 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: In S phase, the association of helicase-activating factors selects a subset of helicase double hexamers to initiate DNA unwinding and form the core of a bidirectional pair of replisomes.
source: In S phase, the association of helicase-activating factors selects a subset of these helicase double hexamers to initiate DNA unwinding and form the core of a bidirectional pair of replisomes (Mantiero et al., 2011; Tanaka et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Helicase activation is the committed step of replication initiation and is controlled during the cell cycle by two kinases: S-CDK and Dbf4-dependent kinase (DDK).
source: Helicase activation is the committed step of replication initiation and is controlled during the cell cycle by two kinases: S-CDK and Dbf4-dependent kinase (DDK) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1; Labib, 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation and reference to a figure.

claim: DDK phosphorylates the long unstructured N-terminal tails of Mcm4 and Mcm6 driving the recruitment of Sld3/7 and Cdc45 to Mcm2-7 double hexamers.
source: DDK phosphorylates the long unstructured N-terminal tails of Mcm4 and Mcm6 driving the recruitment of Sld3/7 and Cdc45 to Mcm2-7 double hexamers (Kamimura et al., 2001; Kanemaki and Labib, 2006; Sheu and Stillman, 2010; Heller et al., 2011; Randell et al., 2010; Deegan et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: S-CDK phosphorylates Sld2 and Sld3/7, leading them to bind to two distinct pairs of BRCT repeats in Dpb11.
source: S-CDK phosphorylates Sld2 and Sld3/7, leading them to bind to two distinct pairs of BRCT repeats in Dpb11 (Tanaka et al., 2007; Zegerman and Diffley, 2007; Muramatsu et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: S-CDK-dependent interactions recruit GINS to Sld3/7 associated with loaded Mcm2-7 complexes.
source: These S-CDK-dependent interactions recruit GINS to Sld3/7 associated with loaded Mcm2-7 complexes.
evidence: This statement is based on established knowledge from previous studies.

claim: Cdc45 and GINS are direct activators of the Mcm2-7 complex, and association of these factors with the core structured region of Mcm2-7 is required to form a pair of Cdc45-Mcm2-7-GINS complexes (CMGs), the active eukaryotic replicative helicase.
source: Cdc45 and GINS are direct activators of the Mcm2-7 complex, and association of these factors with the core structured region of Mcm2-7 is required to form a pair of Cdc45-Mcm2-7-GINS complexes (CMGs), the active eukaryotic replicative helicase (Ilves et al., 2010; Moyer et al., 2006; Pacek et al., 2006; Yuan et al., 2016; Goswami et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: Mcm10 activates CMG complexes to unwind origin DNA.
source: Finally, Mcm10 activates CMG complexes to unwind origin DNA (van Deursen et al., 2012; Kanke et al., 2012; Lõoke et al., 2017; Douglas et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The result of helicase activation is the formation of two oppositely directed, active CMG complexes that generate the ssDNA necessary to recruit the rest of the replisome.
source: The result of this process is the formation of two oppositely directed, active CMG complexes that generate the ssDNA necessary to recruit the rest of the replisome (Bell and Labib, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: There are many Sld3-binding sites on the N-terminal tails of Mcm4 and Mcm6, although a specific binding motif has not been defined.
source: For example, current studies suggest that there are many Sld3-binding sites on the N-terminal tails of Mcm4 and Mcm6, although a specific binding motif has not been defined (Deegan et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Sld3 and Sld7 form a heterotetramer that could facilitate simultaneous recruitment of two Cdc45s.
source: The possibility of coordinated Cdc45 recruitment is raised by evidence suggesting that Sld3 and Sld7 form a heterotetramer that could facilitate simultaneous recruitment of two Cdc45s (Itou et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work and is presented as a possibility.

claim: The levels of DDK and a subset of helicase-activation proteins are known to modulate the timing and efficiency of helicase activation.
source: Lastly, the levels of DDK and a subset of helicase-activation proteins are known to modulate the timing and efficiency of helicase activation (Mantiero et al., 2011; Tanaka et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The circular template exhibited a twofold higher occupancy by Mcm2-7 at the end of a 20-min SM helicase-loading assay compared to a linear template.
source: Comparison of the circular template with a 1.3-kb linear template (Ticau et al., 2015) showed that the circular template exhibited a twofold higher occupancy by Mcm2-74SNAP549 at the end of a 20-min SM helicase-loading assay (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: More than half (0.53 ± 0.04) of the DNAs with loaded Mcm2-74SNAP549 complexes were bound to Cdc45SORT649 when observed immediately after the HSW2 high-salt wash.
source: Consistent with efficient CMG formation, more than half (0.53 ± 0.04) of the DNAs with loaded Mcm2-74SNAP549 complexes were bound to Cdc45SORT649 when observed immediately after the HSW2 high-salt wash (Figure 1B).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: Cdc45 binding events were eliminated in the absence of Sld3/7.
source: These binding events were eliminated in the absence of Sld3/7, consistent with Cdc45SORT649 recruitment to Mcm2-7 relying on Sld3/7 (Figure 1B).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: When Cdc6 was eliminated from the first step of the reaction to prevent helicase loading, subsequent CMG formation was dramatically reduced (fraction of DNAs bound by Cdc45 was 0.12 ± 0.01 with Cdc6 vs. 0.006 ± 0.006 without).
source: Similarly, when Cdc6 was eliminated from the first step of the reaction to prevent helicase loading, subsequent CMG formation was dramatically reduced (fraction of DNAs bound by Cdc45 was 0.12 ± 0.01 with Cdc6 vs. 0.006 ± 0.006 without, Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: In the absence of DDK, high-salt-resistant bound Cdc45 was reduced but not eliminated.
source: In the absence of DDK, high-salt-resistant bound Cdc45 was reduced but not eliminated (Figure 1B).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: DDK-independent binding events are due to residual DDK phosphorylation present on Mcm2-7 complexes purified from G1-arrested cells.
source: We hypothesized that these 'DDK-independent' binding events were due to residual DDK phosphorylation present on Mcm2-7 complexes purified from G1-arrested cells (Heller et al., 2011; Tanaka et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on inference from the data and supported by citations.

claim: Phosphatase treatment of Mcm2-74SNAP549 prior to helicase loading eliminated CMG formation in the absence of DDK.
source: Consistent with this idea, phosphatase treatment of Mcm2-74SNAP549 prior to helicase loading eliminated CMG formation in the absence of DDK (Figure 1B).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: Sequential treatments with phosphatase and DDK rescued CMG formation both in the SM and ensemble settings.
source: We confirmed that phosphatase-treated Mcm2-74SNAP549 remained functional by sequential treatments with phosphatase and DDK. This sequence of treatments rescued CMG formation both in the SM (Figure 1B) and ensemble (Figure 1—figure supplement 5) settings, demonstrating that the observed CMG formation was fully DDK-dependent.
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: A fraction of DNAs with bound Mcm2-74SNAP549 (0.24 ± 0.04) showed increased fluorescence consistent with DNA unwinding.
source: Consistent with previous in vitro assays that showed only a subset of loaded Mcm2-7 are activated (Douglas et al., 2018), we observed increased fluorescence for a fraction of DNAs with bound Mcm2-74SNAP549 (0.24 ± 0.04, Figure 1D).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in a figure and a citation.

claim: Elimination of helicase-activating factors (S-CDK, Cdc45, GINS, Dpb11, Pol ε, Sld3/7, RPA, and Mcm10) from the reaction prevented all unquenching events.
source: Importantly, elimination of helicase-activating factors (S-CDK, Cdc45, GINS, Dpb11, Pol ε, Sld3/7, RPA, and Mcm10) from the reaction prevented all unquenching events (Figure 1D).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: With only Sld3/7 and Cdc45SORT649 added after DDK phosphorylation, dynamic binding of one or two Cdc45SORT649 was detected with the majority of Mcm2-74SNAP549-bound DNA molecules (136/198).
source: Under these conditions, we detected dynamic binding of one or two Cdc45SORT649 with the majority of Mcm2-74SNAP549-bound DNA molecules (136/198, Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: A subset (62/198) of DNAs with loaded Mcm2-74SNAP549 never showed bound Cdc45 in the minimal protein set experiment.
source: A subset (62/198) of DNAs with loaded Mcm2-74SNAP549 never showed bound Cdc45.
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data.

claim: High-salt-resistant Cdc45 binding to Mcm2-7 was not detected (0/70) in the minimal protein set experiment.
source: Consistent with the dynamic nature of the observed Cdc45 interactions and the requirement for additional proteins for CMG formation, in a separate experiment we did not detect high-salt-resistant Cdc45 binding to Mcm2-7 (0/70).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data.

claim: One Cdc45SORT649 was bound to a DNA with an Mcm2-74SNAP549 double hexamer 0.222 ± 0.002 of the time and two Cdc45SORT649 were bound only 0.079 ± 0.001 of the time in the minimal protein set experiment.
source: This analysis showed that one Cdc45SORT649 was bound to a DNA with an Mcm2-74SNAP549 double hexamer 0.222 ± 0.002 of the time and two Cdc45SORT649 were bound only 0.079 ± 0.001 of the time (Supplementary file 1a).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data analysis.

claim: On average, less than one Cdc45 molecule (labeled plus unlabeled) was associated with a loaded Mcm2-7 double hexamer (0.60 ± 0.06) in the minimal protein set experiment.
source: Taking into consideration our finding that 0.73 ± 0.07 of the Cdc45 protein was labeled (see Materials and methods), we found that, on average, less than one Cdc45 molecule (labeled plus unlabeled) was associated with a loaded Mcm2-7 double hexamer (0.60 ± 0.06, Figure 2Ci).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data analysis shown in a figure.

claim: The multiple Cdc45s binding to Mcm2-7-bound DNA are recruited as monomers in a sequential fashion.
source: Thus, we conclude that the multiple Cdc45s binding to Mcm2-7-bound DNA are recruited as monomers in a sequential fashion.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on analysis of fluorescence intensity patterns.

claim: The addition of the SDPGC proteins lowered the fraction of time that DNA molecules bound by Mcm2-74SNAP549 were not associated with Cdc45SORT649 (− SDPGC 0.682 ± 0.001; + SDPGC, 0.560 ± 0.001).
source: Fluorescent analysis showed that the addition of the SDPGC proteins lowered the fraction of time that DNA molecules bound by Mcm2-74SNAP549 were not associated with Cdc45SORT649 (− SDPGC 0.682 ± 0.001; + SDPGC, 0.560 ± 0.001, Supplementary file 1a, rows 1 and 2).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data analysis.

claim: The average number of Cdc45 proteins (labeled plus unlabeled) on a Mcm2-74SNAP549-bound DNA increased with SDPGC proteins (− SDPGC 0.60 ± 0.06; + SDPGC, 0.85 ± 0.08).
source: Consistent with this change, the average number of Cdc45 proteins (labeled plus unlabeled) on a Mcm2-74SNAP549-bound DNA increased in these conditions (− SDPGC 0.60 ± 0.06; + SDPGC, 0.85 ± 0.08, Figure 2Ci, ii).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data analysis shown in a figure.

claim: SM experiments lacking the SDPGC proteins showed no high-salt-resistant Cdc45 binding (0/70).
source: In contrast to SM experiments lacking the SDPGC proteins that showed no high-salt-resistant Cdc45 binding (0/70), the presence of the SDPGC proteins results in a fraction of loaded Mcm2-7 complexes forming the high-salt-resistant Cdc45 complexes characteristic of CMG formation (0.15 ± 0.05, Figure 3A).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: The presence of the SDPGC proteins results in a fraction of loaded Mcm2-7 complexes forming the high-salt-resistant Cdc45 complexes characteristic of CMG formation (0.15 ± 0.05).
source: In contrast to SM experiments lacking the SDPGC proteins that showed no high-salt-resistant Cdc45 binding (0/70), the presence of the SDPGC proteins results in a fraction of loaded Mcm2-7 complexes forming the high-salt-resistant Cdc45 complexes characteristic of CMG formation (0.15 ± 0.05, Figure 3A).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: At higher DDK concentration (6.5 nM), the fraction of Mcm2-74SNAP549-bound DNAs that became bound by high-salt-resistant Cdc45SORT649 increased from 0.15 ± 0.05 to 0.53 ± 0.04.
source: At the higher DDK concentration used in Figure 1 (fivefold increase from 1.3 nM to 6.5 nM), the fraction of Mcm2-74SNAP549-bound DNAs that became bound by high-salt-resistant Cdc45SORT649 increased from 0.15 ± 0.05 to 0.53 ± 0.04 (Figure 3A).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: Elevating DDK concentration to 32.5 nM increased the fraction of loaded Mcm2-7 complexes forming CMGs from 0.53 ± 0.04 to 0.69 ± 0.06.
source: Elevating DDK concentration fivefold further (to 32.5 nM) increased the fraction of loaded Mcm2-7 complexes forming CMGs from 0.53 ± 0.04 to 0.69 ± 0.06 (Figure 3A).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: Elevating DDK levels to 6.5 nM increased the average number of Cdc45 molecules (labeled plus unlabeled) bound to Mcm2-7 by more than twofold (1.0 ± 0.1 vs. 2.5 ± 0.2).
source: Fluorescence-intensity analysis revealed that elevating DDK levels to 6.5 nM increased the average number of Cdc45 molecules (labeled plus unlabeled) bound to Mcm2-7 by more than twofold (1.0 ± 0.1 vs. 2.5 ± 0.2; Figure 3C, compare panels i and ii).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data analysis shown in a figure.

claim: Sometimes four or more Cdc45SORT649 molecules bound to an individual Mcm2-74SNAP549 double hexamer at 6.5 nM DDK.
source: This analysis also revealed sometimes four or more Cdc45SORT649 molecules bound to an individual Mcm2-74SNAP549 double hexamer at 6.5 nM DDK.
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data analysis.

claim: All of the Cdc45SORT649 binding events remain Sld3/7-dependent.
source: Importantly, all of the Cdc45SORT649 binding events remain Sld3/7-dependent, suggesting that the Cdc45SORT649 binding detected requires indirect binding with the Mcm2-7 tails via Sld3/7 (Figure 3Ciii).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: The fraction of DNAs with Mcm2-74SNAP549 bound at least once by Cdc45 is similar between the 1.3 nM (40 out of 48 molecules, 0.83 ± 0.05) and 6.5 nM (71/87, 0.82 ± 0.06) DDK conditions.
source: The fraction of DNAs with Mcm2-74SNAP549 bound at least once by Cdc45 is similar between the 1.3 nM (40 out of 48 molecules, 0.83 ± 0.05) and 6.5 nM (71/87, 0.82 ± 0.06) DDK conditions, indicating that increasing DDK is primarily impacting the number of Cdc45 molecules bound per double hexamer rather than the fraction of double hexamers that are capable of interacting with Cdc45.
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data analysis.

claim: The multiplicity of the bound Cdc45 suggests that binding occurs on the Mcm4 and Mcm6 tails rather than the core of the Mcm2-7 complex.
source: The multiplicity of the bound Cdc45 suggests that binding occurs on the Mcm4 and Mcm6 tails rather than the core of the Mcm2-7 complex.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of more than two Cdc45 molecules binding and knowledge of Mcm2-7 structure.

claim: The core of each Mcm2-7 molecule is thought to have only one site that directly binds Cdc45.
source: The core of each Mcm2-7 molecule is thought to have only one site that directly binds Cdc45 (the site of Cdc45 association in the CMG, Yuan et al., 2016, Goswami et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous structural studies.

claim: There are many Sld3-binding sites on both the Mcm4 and Mcm6 N-terminal tails.
source: In contrast, there are many Sld3-binding sites on both the Mcm4 and Mcm6 N-terminal tails (Deegan et al., 2016), each of which could recruit Cdc45.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: More than two bound Cdc45 molecules indicates that at least a subset of the Cdc45 binding events observed under high DDK conditions reflect Cdc45 binding (via Sld3) to the phosphorylated N-terminal tails.
source: Thus, the appearance of more than two bound Cdc45 molecules indicates that at least a subset (and perhaps most, see below) of the Cdc45 binding events observed under high DDK conditions reflect Cdc45 binding (via Sld3) to the phosphorylated N-terminal tails.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of multiple Cdc45 binding events and knowledge of Mcm2-7 structure.

claim: More than two Cdc45SORT649 proteins were never (0 of 202 examined) observed to remain bound to a Mcm2-7-bound DNA after the HSW2 high-salt wash.
source: Although our intensity model suggests that a given Mcm2-7 is capable of simultaneously binding four or more Cdc45 molecules during the CMG formation reaction (Figure 3Cii), we never (0 of 202 examined) observed that more than two Cdc45SORT649 proteins remained bound to a Mcm2-7-bound DNA after the HSW2 high-salt wash (e.g., Figure 3B, right panel).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: The maximum of two high-salt-resistant Cdc45s is consistent with the interpretation that high-salt resistance indicates that the Cdc45s are incorporated into CMGs.
source: The maximum of two high-salt-resistant Cdc45s is consistent with the interpretation that high-salt resistance indicates that the Cdc45s are incorporated into CMGs (Yeeles et al., 2015).
evidence: This is an interpretation based on experimental data and a citation to previous work.

claim: Only 42/102 (0.41 ± 0.05) of the Mcm2-7-bound DNAs with salt-resistant Cdc45 included two labeled Cdc45s when CMG formation was performed with 6.5 nM DDK.
source: In contrast, we observed that only 42/102 (0.41 ± 0.05) of the Mcm2-7-bound DNAs with salt-resistant Cdc45 included two labeled Cdc45s when CMG formation was performed with 6.5 nM DDK (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: With 1.3 nM DDK, the fraction of Mcm2-7-bound DNAs with salt-resistant Cdc45 that included two labeled Cdc45s drops to 1/7 (0.14 ± 0.13).
source: When the same measurement is performed with 1.3 nM DDK, this fraction drops to 1/7 (0.14 ± 0.13), consistent with lower numbers of bound Cdc45 leading to more frequent formation of a single CMG within the Mcm2-7 double hexamer.
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data.

claim: CMG formation on the two Mcm2-7 complexes in each double hexamer can occur independently.
source: These findings suggest that CMG formation on the two Mcm2-7 complexes in each double hexamer can occur independently.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the analysis of the number of labeled Cdc45s in CMGs.

claim: There was no significant difference in the dwell time distributions of Cdc45SORT649 at 1.3 nM and 6.5 nM DDK.
source: We did not see a significant difference in the dwell time distributions of Cdc45SORT649 at 1.3 nM and 6.5 nM DDK, consistent with the hypothesis that high DDK levels increase the number of Cdc45 associations to Mcm2-7-bound DNA without changing their properties.
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data analysis.

claim: As DDK concentration increases, there is evidence for both increasing numbers of phosphates on the Mcm6 protein and a higher fraction of the molecules being modified.
source: Changes in the mobility of Mcm6 indicated a distribution of numbers of phosphates, arguing against the latter model in which only complete tail phosphorylation occurs. Instead, as DDK concentration increases we see evidence for both increasing numbers of phosphates on the Mcm6 protein and a higher fraction of the molecules being modified.
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data from Phos-tag gels.

claim: A similar experiment with the Mcm4 tail alone also showed elevated numbers of phosphorylation events when DDK concentration was increased.
source: A similar experiment with the Mcm4 tail alone also showed elevated numbers of phosphorylation events when DDK concentration was increased (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: DDK concentration regulates the number of Cdc45 binding through modulation of the number of Mcm4- and Mcm6-tail phosphorylation events.
source: These findings are consistent with DDK concentration regulating the number of Cdc45 binding through modulation of the number of Mcm4- and Mcm6-tail phosphorylation events.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the phosphorylation data.

claim: The fraction of Mcm2-7-DNAs that bound to GINSSORT649 increased when the concentration of DDK was raised from 1.3 to 6.5 nM (0.19 ± 0.04 vs. 0.72 ± 0.04).
source: As we saw with Cdc45, the fraction of Mcm2-7-DNAs that bound to GINSSORT649 increased when the concentration of DDK was raised from 1.3 to 6.5 nM (0.19 ± 0.04 vs. 0.72 ± 0.04; Figure 5A).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: More than two GINSSORT649 were never observed after HSW2.
source: Second, we never observed more than two high-salt-stable GINSSORT649 after HSW2 (Figure 5B), and it is unlikely that we missed additional binding events due to simultaneous photobleaching of two GINSSORT649 molecules (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Elimination of Dpb11 resulted in a complete loss of high-salt-resistant GINS associations.
source: Consistent with this model, we observed a complete loss of high-salt-resistant GINS associations in the absence of Dpb11 (Figure 5A).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: Elimination of Cdc45 (0.09 ± 0.03) or Sld3/7 (0.07 ± 0.02) from the assay resulted in an eightfold to tenfold reduction in high-salt-resistant GINSSORT649 bound to Mcm2-72SORT549-bound DNA.
source: Similarly, elimination of Cdc45 (0.09 ± 0.03) or Sld3/7 (0.07 ± 0.02) from the assay resulted in an eightfold to tenfold reduction in high-salt-resistant GINSSORT649 bound to Mcm2-72SORT549-bound DNA (Figure 5A).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: At 1.3 nM DDK, fluorescence-intensity analysis revealed primarily two or fewer GINSSORT649 molecules binding to a loaded Mcm2-72SORT549 double hexamer.
source: At 1.3 nM DDK, fluorescence-intensity analysis revealed primarily two or fewer GINSSORT649 molecules binding to a loaded Mcm2-72SORT549 double hexamer (Figure 5B, Ci).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data analysis shown in a figure.

claim: At 1.3 nM DDK, the analysis indicated an average of 1.8 ± 0.2 total GINS molecules (labeled plus unlabeled) bound per Mcm2-7-bound DNA.
source: Taking into account the fraction labeled of GINS (0.71 ± 0.07), this analysis indicated an average of 1.8 ± 0.2 total GINS molecules (labeled plus unlabeled) bound per Mcm2-7-bound DNA.
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data analysis.

claim: At 6.5 nM DDK, five or more GINSSORT649 complexes could bind to an Mcm2-72SORT549-DNA complex with an average of 4.3 ± 0.4 GINS (labeled plus unlabeled) per Mcm2-7-bound DNA.
source: In contrast, at 6.5 nM DDK, five or more GINSSORT649 complexes could bind to an Mcm2-72SORT549-DNA complex with an average of 4.3 ± 0.4 GINS (labeled plus unlabeled) per Mcm2-7-bound DNA (Figure 5Cii).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data analysis shown in a figure.

claim: The fraction of DNAs with Mcm2-72SORT549 that bound GINSSORT649 at least once was similar for 1.3 nM (76/84, 0.90 ± 0.04) and 6.5 nM (54/57, 0.95 ± 0.03).
source: As with Cdc45, the fraction of DNAs with Mcm2-72SORT549 that bound GINSSORT649 at least once was similar for 1.3 nM (76/84, 0.90 ± 0.04) and 6.5 nM (54/57, 0.95 ± 0.03).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data.

claim: A dramatic reduction in GINSSORT649 binding events was observed for DNAs that were not associated with a labeled Mcm2-7.
source: As expected, if these interactions occur only on Mcm2-7-bound DNA, we observed a dramatic reduction in GINSSORT649 binding events for DNAs that were not associated with a labeled Mcm2-7 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: Elimination of Dpb11 dramatically reduces the frequency and multiplicity of GINSSORT649 binding to Mcm2-72SORT549.
source: Consistent with models indicating a protein interaction network between Sld3, Dpb11, Sld2 recruits GINS to Mcm2-7, we found that elimination of Dpb11 dramatically reduces the frequency and multiplicity of GINSSORT649 binding to Mcm2-72SORT549 (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: Elimination of either Cdc45 (1.1 ± 0.1) or Sld3/7 (0.7 ± 0.07) resulted in a fourfold reduction in the average number of GINS (labeled plus unlabeled) per Mcm2-7-bound DNA.
source: Elimination of either Cdc45 (1.1 ± 0.1) or Sld3/7 (0.7 ± 0.07) resulted in a fourfold reduction in the average number of GINS (labeled plus unlabeled) per Mcm2-7-bound DNA (Figure 5Ciii, iv).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data analysis shown in a figure.

claim: The initial binding of GINS requires both Sld3/7 and Cdc45 and the recruitment of GINS and Cdc45 occurs via the same Sld3/7 molecules.
source: Thus, we conclude that the initial binding of GINS requires both Sld3/7 and Cdc45 and that the recruitment of GINS and Cdc45 occurs via the same Sld3/7 molecules.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data showing similar effects of Cdc45 and Sld3/7 elimination on GINS binding.

claim: There is a consistent correlation between the multiplicity of GINSSORT649 binding events and the frequency that these events are converted into CMGs.
source: Importantly, we also see a consistent correlation between the multiplicity of GINSSORT649 binding events (Figure 5C) and the frequency that these events are converted into CMGs (Figure 5A).
evidence: This statement is supported by comparison of data shown in figures.

claim: Each of the Mcm2-7 mutants showed a significantly lower fraction of loaded Mcm2-7 molecules that were converted to CMGs when compared to WT Mcm2-7.
source: Each of the Mcm2-7 mutants showed a significantly lower fraction of loaded Mcm2-7 molecules that were converted to CMGs when compared to WT Mcm2-7 (Figure 6A).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: In experiments with 6.5 nM DDK, Mcm4 (0.21 ± 0.07) and Mcm6 (0.30 ± 0.07) mutants reduced the fraction of CMG formation by approximately half relative to WT Mcm2-7.
source: In experiments with 6.5 nM DDK, Mcm4 (0.21 ± 0.07) and Mcm6 (0.30 ± 0.07) mutants reduced this fraction by approximately half relative to WT Mcm2-7, consistent with the elimination of DDK sites on one of the two tails.
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data.

claim: The impact of the Mcm6 tail deletion (0.04 ± 0.02) was substantially larger than that of the Mcm6 phosphorylation mutant.
source: Interestingly, the impact of the Mcm6 tail deletion (0.04 ± 0.02) was substantially larger than that of the Mcm6 phosphorylation mutant.
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data.

claim: The deletion of the Mcm6 tail either eliminates additional phosphorylation sites that impact CMG formation or there are other functions beyond CtG formation performed by the Mcm6 N-terminal tail during helicase activation.
source: This observation suggests that either the deletion eliminates additional phosphorylation sites that impact CMG formation or that there are other functions beyond CtG formation performed by the Mcm6 N-terminal tail during helicase activation (see Discussion).
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observation that the deletion has a larger effect than the phosphorylation mutant.

claim: The average number of Cdc45 (labeled plus unlabeled) bound to Mcm2-74SNAP549-6AD/E+ASP/Q, Mcm2-72SORT549-4AD/E+ASP/Q, or Mcm2-74SNAP549-6ΔN during CMG formation at 6.5 nM DDK was lowered when compared to WT Mcm2-7 (1.7 ± 0.2, 1.5 ± 0.1, and 0.10 ± 0.01, respectively).
source: Fluorescence-intensity analysis revealed that the average number of Cdc45 (labeled plus unlabeled) bound to Mcm2-74SNAP549-6AD/E+ASP/Q, Mcm2-72SORT549-4AD/E+ASP/Q, or Mcm2-74SNAP549-6ΔN during CMG formation at 6.5 nM DDK was also lowered when compared to WT Mcm2-7 (1.7 ± 0.2, 1.5 ± 0.1, and 0.10 ± 0.01, respectively; Figure 6C, Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data analysis shown in figures.

claim: There is a correlation between the impact of the mutants on the multiplicity of CtG events with the efficiency of CMG formation.
source: Thus, as with the protein elimination experiments (e.g., –Sld3/7, –Dpb11, and –Cdc45; Figure 3 and Figure 5), we observe a correlation between the impact of the mutants on the multiplicity of CtG events with the efficiency of CMG formation (compare Figure 6A and C).
evidence: This statement is supported by comparison of data shown in figures.

claim: The Mcm4 and Mcm6 DDK-phosphorylation-site mutants reduce but do not eliminate replication initiation.
source: The sequencing results show that the Mcm4 and Mcm6 DDK-phosphorylation-site mutants reduce but do not eliminate replication initiation.
evidence: This statement is supported by BrdU ChIP-seq data.

claim: Peaks of BrdU sequence reads coincide with locations of known early-initiating replication origins.
source: As expected, peaks of BrdU sequence reads coincide with locations of known early-initiating replication origins (Figure 7A).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: Lower normalized read counts were observed for the Mcm4 and Mcm6 mutant cells relative to wild-type, indicating that both mutants reduce early origin efficiency.
source: Importantly, we observe lower normalized read counts for the Mcm4 and Mcm6 mutant cells relative to wild-type, indicating that both mutants reduce early origin efficiency.
evidence: This statement is supported by BrdU ChIP-seq data.

claim: There is a strong reduction in initiation for both mutants when measuring the average read count for 5000 bp on either side of every yeast origin.
source: We also measured the average read count for 5000 bp on either side of every yeast origin. As we saw for the individual origins, there is a strong reduction in initiation for both mutants in these data (Figure 7B).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: The same mutations that alter CtG and CMG formation in vitro impact replication initiation in vivo.
source: Together, these data indicate that the same mutations that alter CtG and CMG formation in vitro impact replication initiation in vivo, supporting a model in which modulating the ability of Mcm2-7 to form multiple CtG complexes in response to DDK levels alters origin initiation frequency in cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the correlation between in vitro and in vivo data.

claim: The CtG is a new intermediate in the helicase-activation process, which can form at multiple sites on the Mcm2-7 N-terminal tails.
source: The studies presented here provide evidence for a new intermediate in the helicase-activation process, the CtG, which can form at multiple sites on the Mcm2-7 N-terminal tails.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion from the study.

claim: DDK levels modulate the number of CtG intermediates formed per loaded Mcm2-7 complex.
source: We found that DDK levels modulate the number of these intermediates formed per loaded Mcm2-7 complex and that only a subset of CtGs transition to a CMG (Figure 8).
evidence: This is a primary conclusion from the study shown in a model figure.

claim: Only a subset of CtGs transition to a CMG.
source: We found that DDK levels modulate the number of these intermediates formed per loaded Mcm2-7 complex and that only a subset of CtGs transition to a CMG (Figure 8).
evidence: This is a primary conclusion from the study shown in a model figure.

claim: The combination of DDK-modulated CtG multiplicity and inefficient CtG to CMG conversion creates a mechanism that controls replication initiation efficiency by sensitizing helicase activation to DDK activity.
source: We propose that the combination of these properties creates a mechanism that controls replication initiation efficiency by sensitizing helicase activation to DDK activity.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the study's findings.

claim: Sld3 contains a phosphopeptide-binding domain that recognizes both DDK-dependent and DDK-independent phosphorylation sites on Mcm4 and Mcm6 N-terminal tails.
source: Previous studies found that Sld3 contains a phosphopeptide-binding domain that recognizes both DDK-dependent and DDK-independent phosphorylation sites on Mcm4 and Mcm6 N-terminal tails (Deegan et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Binding of Sld3 to the DDK-dependent phosphorylation sites is required for the recruitment of Cdc45 to the Mcm2-7 double hexamer.
source: Binding of Sld3 to the DDK-dependent phosphorylation sites is required for the recruitment of Cdc45 to the Mcm2-7 double hexamer (Deegan et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The initial recruitment of GINS and Cdc45 involves formation of a multi-protein complex with the Mcm2-7 N-terminal tails.
source: Here, we present evidence that the initial recruitment of GINS and Cdc45 involves formation of a multi-protein complex with the Mcm2-7 N-terminal tails.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion from the study.

claim: The CtG is an intermediate on the way to CMG formation.
source: Our evidence also supports the CtG being an intermediate on the way to CMG formation.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the study's findings.

claim: Elimination of factors that promote CtG formation (e.g., DDK and Sld3/7) also inhibits CMG formation.
source: Consistent with this hypothesis, elimination of factors that promote CtG formation (e.g., DDK and Sld3/7) also inhibits CMG formation (Figure 1B, Figure 5A).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Elimination of a subset of CtG binding sites by eliminating Mcm4 or Mcm6 DDK-phosphorylation or deleting the Mcm6 N-terminal tail results in a strong reduction in CMG formation that correlates with the effects on CtG formation.
source: Similarly, elimination of a subset of CtG binding sites by eliminating Mcm4 or Mcm6 DDK-phosphorylation or deleting the Mcm6 N-terminal tail results in a strong reduction in CMG formation that correlates with the effects on CtG formation (Figure 6).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: Throughout the studies, a consistent correlation is observed between the multiplicity of CtG formation on a Mcm2-7 double hexamer and the efficiency of subsequent CMG formation.
source: Indeed, throughout our studies we observe a consistent correlation between the multiplicity of CtG formation on a Mcm2-7 double hexamer and the efficiency of subsequent CMG formation.
evidence: This is a summary statement of a pattern observed across multiple experiments.

claim: It is possible that there are additional non-DDK-dependent phosphorylation sites in Mcm6 that are contributing to CtG and CMG formation.
source: It is possible that there are additional non-DDK-dependent phosphorylation sites in Mcm6 that are contributing to CtG and CMG formation, and their elimination by the deletion further reduces the formation of these complexes (Figure 6, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a speculation to explain the larger effect of the deletion compared to the phosphorylation mutant.

claim: Forming CtGs on both the Mcm4 and Mcm6 N-terminal tails, rather than only on the Mcm4 tail, may be advantageous for CMG formation.
source: It is also possible that forming CtGs on both the Mcm4 and Mcm6 N-terminal tails, rather than only on the Mcm4 tail, is advantageous for CMG formation.
evidence: This is a speculation about the function of CtGs on both tails.

claim: The Mcm6 N-terminal tail could facilitate the CtG to CMG transition.
source: A second possibility is that there is an additional function of the Mcm6 tail that contributes to CMG formation. For example, the Mcm6 N-terminal tail could facilitate the CtG to CMG transition.
evidence: This is a speculation about an additional function of the Mcm6 tail.

claim: The Mcm6 N-terminal deletion is not lethal in vivo.
source: We note, however, that such functions cannot be essential since the Mcm6 N-terminal deletion is not lethal in vivo (Champasa et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The CtG minimally includes Cdc45 and GINS bound to Mcm6 and Mcm4 N-terminal tails.
source: Although our findings indicate that the CtG minimally includes Cdc45 and GINS bound to Mcm6 and Mcm4 N-terminal tails, this complex is likely to contain other proteins involved in CMG formation.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the study's findings.

claim: The CtG is likely to contain other proteins involved in CMG formation beyond Cdc45 and GINS.
source: Although our findings indicate that the CtG minimally includes Cdc45 and GINS bound to Mcm6 and Mcm4 N-terminal tails, this complex is likely to contain other proteins involved in CMG formation.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the study's findings and knowledge of CMG formation.

claim: The robust Sld3/7 dependence of Cdc45 and GINS binding to Mcm2-7 suggests that the CtG includes Sld3/7.
source: The robust Sld3/7 dependence of Cdc45 and GINS binding to Mcm2-7 (Figure 3, Figure 5) suggests that the CtG includes this protein.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data shown in figures.

claim: A network of interactions between Sld3, Dpb11, Sld2, and GINS is required to form the CMG.
source: A network of interactions between Sld3, Dpb11, Sld2, and GINS is required to form the CMG (Tanaka et al., 2007; Zegerman and Diffley, 2007; Muramatsu et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The simplest model is that Sld3, Dpb11, Sld2, and GINS are required to form CtGs, and subsequently CMGs.
source: Given Sld3's known binding to phosphorylated N-terminal tails (Deegan et al., 2016), the simplest model is that these interacting proteins are required to form CtGs, and subsequently CMGs.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the study's findings and previous work.

claim: It is possible that Pol ε is simultaneously recruited with GINS to the CtG as part of a preformed pre-LC complex.
source: Finally, it is possible that Pol ε is simultaneously recruited with GINS to the CtG as part of a preformed pre-LC complex (Muramatsu et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a speculation based on previous work.

claim: Dpb11 (and perhaps Sld2 and Pol ε) allows GINS to interact with loaded Mcm2-7 at a low level independently of Cdc45 and Sld3/7.
source: One interesting explanation for this distinction is that Dpb11 (and perhaps Sld2 and Pol ε) allows GINS to interact with loaded Mcm2-7 at a low level independently of Cdc45 and Sld3/7.
evidence: This is a speculation to explain the stronger effect of Dpb11 elimination on GINS binding.

claim: The requirement of Cdc45 to recruit GINS strongly suggests that the CtG involves direct interactions between these proteins.
source: Finally, the requirement of Cdc45 to recruit GINS (Figure 5Ciii) strongly suggests that the CtG involves direct interactions between these proteins, suggesting the interesting possibility that key interactions between these proteins involved in the CMG are already present in the CtG.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: The conversion from CtG to CMG is inefficient.
source: Our studies indicate that the conversion from CtG to CMG is inefficient.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the study's findings.

claim: With low DDK levels, two Cdc45 proteins were often observed to associate with Mcm2-7 double hexamers over long periods of time (>100 s; 33 long-lived binding events/48 double hexamers), but only 7 of these 33 converted to CMGs.
source: With low DDK levels, we often observed two Cdc45 proteins that associated with Mcm2-7 double hexamers over long periods of time (>100 s; 33 long-lived binding events/48 double hexamers). However, only 7 of these 33 converted to CMGs (Figure 3A), indicating that most of the CtGs either dissociate or fail to become part of the CMG before the end of the experiment (Figure 8, top).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: The inefficient conversion of CtGs to CMGs is hypothesized to be true at all DDK concentrations.
source: We hypothesize that this inefficient conversion is true at all DDK concentrations.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the study's findings.

claim: Increased DDK is not associated with a significant change in dwell times of individual Cdc45 molecules or the fraction of Mcm2-7 double hexamers bound by Cdc45 or GINS.
source: In contrast, increased DDK is not associated with a significant change in dwell times of individual Cdc45 molecules (Figure 4) or the fraction of Mcm2-7 double hexamers bound by Cdc45 or GINS.
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: Due to the inefficient conversion of CtGs to CMGs, the increased multiplicity of CtGs on a given double hexamer at higher DDK levels leads to increased opportunities for CtG conversion to CMG and increased rates of origin activation.
source: Based on these findings, we propose that, due to the inefficient conversion of CtGs to CMGs, the increased multiplicity of CtGs on a given double hexamer at higher DDK levels leads to increased opportunities for CtG conversion to CMG (Figure 8, bottom) and, therefore, increased rates of origin activation.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the study's findings shown in a figure.

claim: Increasing the expression of a subset of limiting helicase-activation proteins, including the Dbf4 regulatory subunit of DDK, increased origin initiation efficiency and advanced the time of replication initiation for late initiating origins.
source: These studies showed that increasing the expression of a subset of limiting helicase-activation proteins, including the Dbf4 regulatory subunit of DDK, increased origin initiation efficiency and advanced the time of replication initiation for late initiating origins.
evidence: This statement refers to previous studies on origin initiation control.

claim: The changes in origin initiation efficiency and timing would increase the number of CtGs formed per double hexamer and consequently the efficiency of CMG formation.
source: Our findings suggest that these changes would increase the number of CtGs formed per double hexamer and consequently the efficiency of CMG formation.
evidence: This is an inference connecting the study's findings to previous observations.

claim: The combination of multiple potential phosphorylation sites on the Mcm4 and Mcm6 tails, and the inefficient conversion of the CtGs formed on the tails to the CMG, tunes the helicase-activation process to respond to levels of DDK and other helicase-activation factors.
source: We propose that the combination of multiple potential phosphorylation sites on the Mcm4 and Mcm6 tails, and the inefficient conversion of the CtGs formed on the tails to the CMG, tunes the helicase-activation process to respond to levels of DDK and other helicase-activation factors.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the study's findings.

claim: Reducing the number of phosphorylation sites on Mcm4 and Mcm6 or deleting the Mcm6 tail reduced CtG and CMG formation at the same DDK levels.
source: Consistent with this model, reducing the number of phosphorylation sites on Mcm4 and Mcm6 or deleting the Mcm6 tail reduced CtG and CMG formation at the same DDK levels (Figure 6).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: The same mutations independently reduce origin initiation efficiency in vivo.
source: Importantly, we see that the same mutations independently reduce origin initiation efficiency in vivo (Figure 7).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: Reducing the ability to form CtGs recalibrates the response of origins of replication to DDK levels.
source: These observations strongly suggest that reducing the ability to form CtGs recalibrates the response of origins of replication to DDK levels.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the correlation between in vitro and in vivo data.

claim: The proposed mechanism is analogous to the regulation of Sic1 proteolysis by CDK.
source: Our proposed mechanism (Figure 8) is analogous to the regulation of Sic1 proteolysis by CDK (Nash et al., 2001).
evidence: This is an analogy to another biological system supported by a citation.

claim: Multiple CDK phosphorylation sites on Sic1 are each weakly recognized by the Cdc4 F-box protein, leading to ubiquitinylation and degradation of Sic1.
source: Multiple CDK phosphorylation sites on Sic1 are each weakly recognized by the Cdc4 F-box protein, leading to ubiquitinylation and degradation of Sic1.
evidence: This statement describes the Sic1 system as an analogy.

claim: The accumulation of multiple phosphorylation sites on Sic1 promotes a switch-like response to CDK levels.
source: Although weakly bound, the accumulation of multiple phosphorylation sites on Sic1 promotes a switch-like response to CDK levels.
evidence: This statement describes the Sic1 system as an analogy.

claim: Similar mechanisms are operating during helicase activation, with the Mcm4 and Mcm6 tails providing the multiple phosphorylation-dependent binding sites and the inefficient conversion of the CtG to the CMG performing the role analogous to the suboptimal Cdc4 interaction.
source: We propose that the similar mechanisms are operating during helicase activation, with the Mcm4 and Mcm6 tails providing the multiple phosphorylation-dependent binding sites and the inefficient conversion of the CtG to the CMG performing the role analogous to the suboptimal Cdc4 interaction.
evidence: This is a proposed model drawing an analogy to the Sic1 system.

claim: Processes beyond those shown in Figure 8 are likely to play important roles in origin activation.
source: Processes beyond those shown in Figure 8 are likely to play important roles in origin activation.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment that the model may not be complete.

claim: Phosphatases that could counteract the action of DDK and CDK were not included in the experiments.
source: For example, our experiments did not include phosphatases that could counteract the action of DDK and CDK.
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental design.

claim: Phosphatases might be recruited by Rif1, a protein that interacts with protein phosphatase 1 and has been implicated in the regulation of replication initiation.
source: Such phosphatases might be recruited by Rif1, a protein that interacts with protein phosphatase 1 and has been implicated in the regulation of replication initiation (Hafner et al., 2018; Hiraga et al., 2014; Hiraga et al., 2018; Mattarocci et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a speculation based on previous work.

claim: The presence of phosphatases could regulate Mcm2-7 N-terminal tail phosphorylation levels, further sensitizing origin activation to changes in DDK level.
source: The presence of phosphatases could regulate Mcm2-7 N-terminal tail phosphorylation levels, further sensitizing origin activation to changes in DDK level.
evidence: This is a speculation about the role of phosphatases.

claim: Phosphatases may be essential to remove Mcm2-7-tail phosphorylation after helicase activation to ensure that the tails of active helicases do not continue to compete for limiting helicase-activation factors.
source: In addition, phosphatases may be essential to remove Mcm2-7-tail phosphorylation after helicase activation to ensure that the tails of active helicases do not continue to compete for limiting helicase-activation factors.
evidence: This is a speculation about another potential role of phosphatases.
